summary: Little Sable Point's brick tower, begun in 1873, showed its third-order Fresnel light from 1874 until the Coast Guard decommissioned the navigation light in 2013.

light.relit: 2014, for historical display only (Coast Guard permission)
light.characteristic: fixed white with one white flash every 30 seconds (lens rotated until 1954; single flash by solenoid after 1954)

lens.note: Third-order Fresnel lens by L. Sautter & Cie., Paris (HSR printed p. 14; the tower still houses a third-order lens, HSR p. 31).

structures.note: Double-wall brick tower, begun April 1873 and lit 1874; over 100 ft from base to lantern (HSR p. 31). Unpainted brick until 1900 paint (LighthouseFriends) and whitewash ordered 1875 (HSR); sandblasted 1977 (HSR) or 1974 (LighthouseFriends).
One-and-a-half storey per HSR; twelve rooms over two and a half storeys per LighthouseFriends. Demolished in 1955 (HSR) or torn down in 1958 (LighthouseFriends).
Circular iron oil house, 360 gallons, 100 ft northeast of the tower (Light-House Board 1893). Demolished in 1955 with the other station buildings (HSR).

access.note: In Silver Lake State Park; reached by a paved road. LighthouseFriends: tower open Tuesday to Sunday, 10 a.m. to 5 p.m., late May to early September; call or check the association's website.

corrections.why: The Historic Structures Report (2015) says the Coast Guard decommissioned the navigation light in 2013 and in 2014 allowed it to be lit for historical display. LighthouseFriends gives 2014 as the deactivation year. For human review.

The HSR says the single white flash after 1954 was every thirty seconds; LighthouseFriends says the rotating lens flashed every thirty seconds. The record's six-second figure is not supported by either source read. For human review.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Sources differ on whether the light is lit. The report says the navigation light was decommissioned in 2013 and the Coast Guard allowed the tower to be lit for historical display in 2014; it is not a navigation light now.

notes_for_editor: Newspapers: Chronicling America returned no Michigan newspaper pages for 'Little Sable' with lighthouse, 1874-1922 (searched). The Historic Structures Report is the main source; it is a 2015 consultant's report, and its facts are cited by printed page with paraphrase. The NRHP nomination (84001827) is not digitised in the NPS copy, so the nomination text was not read; the HSR's own appendix F nomination was not separately read. Disagreements left open: dwelling size (one and a half storeys, HSR; twelve rooms over two and a half storeys, LighthouseFriends); dwelling demolition (1955, HSR; 1958, LighthouseFriends); sandblasting (1977, HSR; 1974, LighthouseFriends); electrification (proposed May 1954 and completed December 1954, HSR; LighthouseFriends implies 1953 by 'one year after'); the Board's first recommendation (1870 annual report, HSR; 1871 note, LighthouseFriends); the 1875 whitewash order (HSR) against the 1900 painting (LighthouseFriends); the Armistice Day storm (LighthouseFriends: 92 mph gusts and 30-ft waves; the Pentwater marker: 75 mph and 20-ft waves); the death toll (LighthouseFriends: 56 for Davock and Minch; MSRA: 32 on Davock and the marker's total of 59 seamen). Positions: MSRA places the Davock 1.9 miles off the light but says she sank off Pentwater; the Minch is placed about 1.5 miles south of Pentwater, which is some miles north of the light, so LighthouseFriends' 'off Little Sable Point' for the Minch is doubtful. The 1893 and 1894 Light-House Board entries are for Petite Pointe au Sable only; the Grande Pointe au Sable entries (a different station, with its own life-saving station) were excluded. No life-saving station is recorded at Little Sable. The 2015 HSR describes the Pride wreck only in the chronology. Fact-check 2026-10-22 additions: the Light-House Board entries are labelled by fiscal year (ended 30 June 1893 and 1894). The Michigan Shipwreck Research Association gives the Davock as 1.9 miles off the light, but its own coordinates (N 43 40.367, W 086 36.335) lie about 3.6 statute miles from the report's light coordinates (N 43 39 04.9, W 86 32 22.3); the story reports the Association's figure as its figure and does not repeat the distance as settled. The Minch bow coordinates (N 43 45.784) put her about 6.7 nautical miles north of the light's coordinates, so LighthouseFriends' 'off Little Sable Point' does not match the Association's position; the story says so. Distances at sea are converted to nautical miles as the guide asks (statute miles in the sources). Keeper lines were checked against roster.py (45 lines, all matched with person slugs).
